name: Saint Barnabas the Apostle
history: A Levite from Cyprus named Joseph, whom the apostles called Barnabas, son of encouragement. He sold a field and laid the money at their feet, vouched for Saul when the Church in Jerusalem feared him, and later brought him to Antioch. Together they made the first great missionary journey. Tradition says Barnabas was martyred in Cyprus.
life: The Acts of the Apostles calls Barnabas a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. When the new convert Saul came to Jerusalem and the disciples were afraid of him, Barnabas took him to the apostles and told how he had preached boldly in Damascus. Sent to Antioch, where Gentiles were turning to the Lord, Barnabas rejoiced, then went to Tarsus to find Saul and bring him to help. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians. The Holy Spirit set the two apart, and they sailed to Cyprus and on into Asia Minor. Later they disagreed sharply over taking Barnabas’s cousin John Mark with them, and parted, Barnabas taking Mark to Cyprus. Paul later speaks warmly of both. Tradition holds that Barnabas was stoned at Salamis.
prayerTo: Saint Barnabas, son of encouragement, you saw good in Saul when others saw only danger, and you gave a second chance to Mark. Pray for me, that I may be generous with my goods and with my trust, and that my words may build others up in Christ. Amen.
penance: Encourage someone today in a specific way, by a note, a call or a word of thanks, and give alms in memory of the field Barnabas sold.
meditation: Without Barnabas, Saul might have been left alone. Whom could you stand beside who has been kept at a distance?
prayer: O God, Who gladden us by the merits and intercession of blessed Barnabas, Your Apostle, mercifully grant that we, who ask Your favors through him, may obtain them by the gift of Your grace. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
